title: Examining axion-like particles with superconducting radio-frequency cavity
relevance: Prints the exact retarded KG kernel with mass tail used by the response-memory contract; nearest prior work for the support statement.
limits: Selected AppendixA and source comparison only; harmonic-source calculation is a single-frequency steady state, not a worst-case bounded-history norm. No such norm found in inspected passages; no exhaustive absence claim about the paper.
version: JHEP03(2021)143, DOI 10.1007/JHEP03(2021)143, arXiv:2011.12871; received 2020-12-10, accepted 2021-02-08, published 2021-03-15; SCOAP3 open access PDF fetched from link.springer.com on 2026-10-30.
section_locator: Appendix A 'Retarded Green function', printed p. 15: eq. (A.1) kernel G_ret = (1/4pi)[delta(t-t'-R)/R - theta(t-t'-R)(m_a/u) J1(m_a u)], u = sqrt((t-t')^2 - R^2); eq. (A.2) harmonic-source integral attributed to Gradshteyn-Ryzhik [49]; eq. (A.3) steady-state response. Kernel authority cited as [48] Polyanin, Handbook of linear partial differential equations, CRC Press (2016).
assumptions: Classical retarded Klein-Gordon field in 3+1 Minkowski for a massive pseudoscalar coupled to two harmonic cavity modes; prescribed EM source E.B; retarded boundary condition (no incoming free field).
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: the produced axion field for harmonic sources is (2.3)-(2.4), mass enters through e^{i R k} vs e^{-R kappa}; massless term is the delta/R light-cone part of (A.1), so the mass dependence is entirely the tail term.
proof_status: Established standard physics; (A.1) is a textbook retarded Green function (authors cite a handbook, not a proof paper); their derivations (A.2)-(A.3) are routine integrals verified here by inspection at full-text depth.
open_questions: Does Polyanin (2016), or any accessible edition lineage of it, print an L1-kernel-mass or operator-norm comparison of the massive vs massless retarded kernel? (paywalled print; unresolved).

title: Fading Memory and the Problem of Approximating Nonlinear Operators with Volterra Series
relevance: Defines the fading-memory framework; Theorem 5 identifies LTI fading-memory operators with bounded convolution measures on R+, which contains both R_m and R_0 as instances; The discussion preceding Theorem6 in§8.2 states the already-known realization independence; Theorem6 itself concerns unique steady state.
limits: No mass parameter, no Bessel kernels, no kernel-support statement, no small-parameter norm comparison of two kernels; approximation is peak-error worst case over bounded slew-limited sets K, not over our L-infinity ball of source histories. Fading-memory realization invariance is already known here and is not a candidate result.
version: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems, vol. CAS-32, no. 11, pp. 1150-1161, Nov. 1985, DOI 10.1109/TCS.1985.1085649; author-hosted published PDF (web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/pdf/fading_volterra.pdf) fetched 2026-10-30; pagination matches the journal version.
section_locator: Section III pp. 1152-1153: FM definition eq. (3.1), weighted norm eq. (3.2), Remarks 1-4; Section IV Theorem 1 (Volterra approximation) with K from eq. (4.1); Section V Theorem 2; Section VIII: 8.1 Theorem 5 'Convolution Theorem' p. 1157 (I) LTI+FM iff convolution with bounded measure h on R+ (may contain delta-functions), (II) discrete-time analog; 8.2 Theorem 6 pp. 1157-1158 (Theorem6: FM implies unique steady state; preceding discussion: FM is an I/O property independent of realization); Conclusion p. 1158: approximation 'in the sense of peak error, worst case for all signals in K'.
assumptions: Time invariance, causality, continuity strengthened to fading memory (weighted-norm continuity of the associated functional); signal sets bounded and slew-limited in continuous time.
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: any TI operator with fading memory is uniformly approximable by a finite Volterra series operator, realizable as a finite-dimensional exponentially stable linear system with polynomial readout, for all time; LTI+FM equals convolution with a bounded measure.
proof_status: Established, peer-reviewed 1985; proofs in Appendices A1-A5 read at full-text depth; no correspondence to KG kernels attempted or needed.
dependencies: Volterra 1959 p.188 and Wiener 1958 p.89 (concept history, quoted at abstract level in the paper)
open_questions: None for this lane; the bounded-measure framework suffices to classify the candidate norm statement as a folklore-corollary setting.

title: The zero mass problem for Klein-Gordon equations
relevance: Nearest uniform-in-mass estimate line for Klein-Gordon; establishes that 'uniform mass estimates' are an established research subject, in a different problem class (Cauchy decay, not retarded response norms).
limits: Scope nonmatch for the audited claims: global decay of small compact-support Cauchy data for a coupled nonlinear wave-KG system; no retarded Green function, no kernel operator norm, no support statement, no prescribed-source worst-case class. This v1 is a preprint (May 2019); later published versions were not consulted.
version: arXiv:1905.08620v1 [math.AP], submitted 21 May 2019 (exact v1 PDF fetched from arxiv.org on 2026-10-30).
section_locator: Abstract; Section 1 Introduction incl. Theorem 1.1 (p. 2 of v1 PDF: |u(t,x)| <~ 1/(t + m t^{3/2})); Section 3.1 Proposition 3.1 (|w| <~ eps min{(t+2)^{-1}, m^{-1}(t+2)^{-3/2}}); Section 3.2 Proposition 3.3 (L2 uniform-in-m estimates via frequency-space Hardy inequality); Section 5 proof of Theorem 1.1.
assumptions: m in [0,1]; smallness ||u0,v0||_{H^{N+1}} + ||u1,v1||_{H^N} <= eps with N >= 14, compactly supported data at t0 = 2; coupled wave-KG nonlinearities with constants independent of m; Minkowski 3+1.
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: first rigorous proof of unified-in-m decay for the model system, |u| <~ 1/(t + m t^{3/2}), |v| <~ t^{-3/2+delta}.
proof_status: Peer-preprint claim (v1); proof structure (contraction + hyperboloidal energy) read at full-text depth for statement-level correspondence only; correctness not independently re-verified in this lane.
dependencies: LeFloch-Ma hyperboloidal foliation method (cited [15],[16], not read this lane)
open_questions: Whether any published successor of this v1 (e.g., Dong's later papers or LeFloch's program) contains a retarded-kernel norm estimate as mass goes to zero; outside this lane's two-batch budget.

title: NIST DLMF §10.7 Limiting Forms (Bessel functions), eq. 10.7.3
authors: NIST DLMF (D.W. Lozier et al., eds.)
relevance: Small-argument form J_nu(z)~(z/2)^nu/Gamma(nu+1) gives J1(z)=O(z) near zero and the integrability input. A finite-argument bound requires the separate Poisson-integral entry10.9.4, directly checked by coordinator.
limits: Used only for the two asymptotic inputs; no support or norm content.
version: Live official DLMF HTML retrieved30October2026; exact cited equation identifiers, no release-number assertion.
section_locator: §10.7(i) z->0, eq. 10.7.3 (J_nu limiting form), with note attributing (10.7.3) to (10.2.2) and (10.8.2).
conclusion: J1(z)/z tends to1/2 at zero. This asymptotic alone does not give a bound on an entire prescribed finite interval.

title: NIST DLMF §10.17 Asymptotic Expansions for Large Argument (Bessel functions), Hankel expansions
authors: NIST DLMF (D.W. Lozier et al., eds.)
relevance: Large-argument Hankel expansion gives |J1(z)| = O(z^{-1/2}), hence |J1(z)|/z = O(z^{-3/2}) integrable at infinity: finiteness of C_* = int_0^inf |J1(z)|/z dz.
limits: Leading-order accuracy only used in the 0.06 s numerical sanity check; not a precision computation.
version: Live official DLMF HTML retrieved30October2026; exact cited equation identifiers, no release-number assertion.
section_locator: §10.17(i), eqs. 10.17.1-10.17.3 (expansion for J_nu(z), large real z).
conclusion: |J1(z)| <~ sqrt(2/(pi z)) for large z (leading term), so C_* < infinity.
open_questions: Exact closed form of C_* unknown to this lane; not needed for the verdict.
